newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKEY-CRONJE TO CAPTAIN IRISH CRICKET TEAM.
newsitem.headline: CRICKEY-CRONJE TO CAPTAIN IRISH CRICKET TEAM.

text.p: South African cricket captain Hansie Cronje is to lead Ireland in England's Benson and Hedges Cup limited-overs competition later this year, it was revealed on Monday.
Cronje, who has never been to Ireland, will captain the side in four matches starting in April in a competition where they have not won a game since they first participated in 1994.

Ireland's most famous cricketing victory came in a one-day game at the expense of the mighty West Indies in 1969 and, with the inspirational Cronje at the helm, they now hope to win at least one group match.
Cronje, who played for Leicestershire in 1995, will be sponsored by the Independent Newspaper group, an Irish group which owns newspapers in South Africa.
The idea, though, was proposed by Ali Bacher, managing director of the United Cricket Board of South Africa and chairman of the International Cricket Council's (ICC's) development committee.
"I visited Ireland in August and it is one of the seven countries the ICC has targeted for immediate assistance to help spread the game globally," said Bacher.
"There is a strong cricketing culture in Ireland, where the game has been played for more than a hundred years, but it has a low profile and the base is small.
Cronje, who will also take an active part in coaching clinics and promoting the game, said he was looking forward to the new role.
"I've never been to Ireland before but I hope I can give their cricket a big boost -- I certainly don't mind the odd pint of Guinness!"
